title: I Printed the Billiards-Table Hour After the Manager's Cousin Camped It

parts.text: I paid table 5 at 8:12 p.m. and manager Faye's cousin was still racking on my light. The lamp said: PAY THE LIGHT. SIXTY MINUTES. NO FAMILY HOLDS. I was twenty-four, walk-in, holding a time card. Faye shrugged. "Cousins are the hall." I photographed the lamp, the card, and the cousin's rack on my coins. Then I asked for the table log. At 8:18 the owner pinged why Faye's name was on a held light. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The owner can see Faye's cousin racking on table 5 during my paid light.

social.video_title: The manager's cousin camped my paid table light — Part 1/2
social.description: Billiards, a sixty-minute lamp, a family hold. I logged the rack. Would you have asked for the table log?

parts.text: Faye called it a lesson until the owner asked for the still. I printed the log, the lamp, and the card. The cousin paid. Faye ran lights like everyone else and told the next manager lessons were always about optics. Optics is a word managers use when coins exist. Hour policy now has a second line: COUSINS PAY THE LIGHT. I keep table 5. Faye brown-bags her jokes. The hall finally looks like a card, not a living room. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Table log, a paid cousin, and a second line. Was a lesson ever my coins?
